extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and applicants interacting with USPTO procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Change-summary extract of MPEP (9th edition, Rev. 07.2022) detailing updated procedural and substantive rules for patent examination (IDSs, RCEs, interviews, abandonment, restriction practice, double-patenting, affidavits/declarations, etc.). Intended to guide how examiners and practitioners comply with and apply updated MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) content and timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on what constitutes compliant IDS content and the timing for filing IDSs (including handling omissions and timing when deadlines fall on weekends/holidays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bona fide attempt is made to comply with IDS content requirements but part of the required content is inadvertently omitted, additional time may be given to enable full compliance. When no page numbers are supplied in an IDS, it is understood that all of the pages of the publication are the relevant pages. Clarified requirements for seeking consideration of documents other than the specification and drawings of a pending U.S. application cited in an IDS. The publisher of an Internet-obtained publication may be evident from the URL (see MPEP § 707.05(e)). There is no requirement for a copy of each U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication listed in an IDS unless required by the Office. Circumstances under which electronic means/medium for filing IDSs is permitted are clarified. An IDS may be timely filed on the next succeeding business day if the last day of the three-month period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(b)(1) and (b)(2) falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or a federal holiday in D.C. An IDS filed on the same day as or after the mailing date of an Ex parte Quayle action or notice of appeal must comply with 37 CFR 1.97(d). An IDS filed after the examiner has reached a final determination on patentability of the claims will be handled by the examiner as a “Printer Rush” per MPEP § 1309.02. A statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e) may be timely filed on the next succeeding business day if the last day falls on a weekend/holiday.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time and bona fide attempt (37 CFR 1.97(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural guidance on extensions of time related to IDSs and the treatment of bona fide attempts to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection amended to clarify extensions of time (37 CFR 1.97(f)) and to incorporate the concept of a bona fide attempt; related form paragraph relocations noted. (Section moved and reorganized in MPEP § 609.04(b), subsection VI.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review of prior examiner's search
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should review searches performed by previous examiners to ensure the search was thorough and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised to clarify that an examiner should review the search of a previous examiner to ensure the search is thorough and complete and added a cross reference to MPEP § 904.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE (Request for Continued Examination) processing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and limitations when processing an RCE, including documentation verification and situations where an RCE will not be processed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support personnel verify that a compliant inventor’s oath or declaration for each inventor was submitted prior to or with the RCE for national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371. An RCE will not be processed if the application is undergoing court review at the Federal Circuit or in federal district court (cross-reference to subsection XII). Applicants cannot use an RCE to switch inventions as a matter of right (see 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP § 706.07(h)). Added sentences regarding additional time periods during which an RCE may be timely filed after a new ground of rejection was made by the Board and after a request for rehearing; res judicata applies to new grounds and any other rejection affirmed in a Board decision when an RCE is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling IDSs filed after final/Printer Rush processing
rubrics_metrics.description: How IDSs filed after an examiner’s final determination are handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS filed after the examiner has reached a final determination on the patentability of the claims will be handled by the examiner as a “Printer Rush” per MPEP § 1309.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of non-patent documents with lengthy citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for examiners on citing non-patent documents that have lengthy citations on form PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changed title to “Non-Patent Documents Having a Lengthy Citation” and added guidance regarding how examiners should cite non-patent documents having lengthy citations on form PTO-892. Revised related form paragraphs (7.37.05, 7.37.07, 7.37.08).

rubrics_metrics.name: Returned Office action mailing and reply period reset guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a returned Office action will be mailed and when it is appropriate to reset or restart a reply period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised where a returned Office action will be mailed if the Office action was originally mailed to the correct correspondence address, and added a cross reference to MPEP § 710.06 for when it is appropriate to reset or restart a reply period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination acceptance limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Cap on the number of prioritized examination requests accepted in a fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised reproduced text of 37 CFR 1.102 to reflect that 15,000 requests for prioritized examination could be accepted in any fiscal year; corresponding changes elsewhere in the MPEP to reflect 15,000-per-fiscal-year limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103
rubrics_metrics.description: When USPTO may grant suspension of action and examples of good and insufficient cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added sentences stating that the USPTO may grant a suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a) for a specified period not to exceed six months; added examples explaining what may be considered good and sufficient cause and examples of what may not be considered good and sufficient cause. Also clarified that after expiration of a suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(d) the application will automatically be queued for docketing based upon the order in which it was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for suspension/extension decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Who decides suspensions or extensions of action under particular regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaced references to ‘TC Director of work group 3640’ with ‘TC Director who oversees Licensing and Review’ when discussing who decides a suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(f) and similarly for extensions under 35 U.S.C. 267.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt dates, abandonment, and petitions to revive
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for recording receipt dates, abandonment consequences, calculation of last days when periods fall on weekends/holidays, and petition-to-revive requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of receipt of a reply to an Office action is recorded in the electronic file as the receipt date of the reply paper. Failure to file a reply during the shortened statutory period results in abandonment unless the time is extended under 37 CFR 1.136. Added Juneteenth (June 19) to list of federal holidays and examples for calculating last day when due date falls on weekend/holiday (cross reference to MPEP § 711.04(a)). An application is abandoned when an amendment is filed after expiration of the statutory period and is not timely under 35 U.S.C. 21 and 37 CFR 1.7; the examiner should notify the applicant or attorney/agent of record that the application has been abandoned. A petition to revive is under 37 CFR 1.137; any applicant filing a petition to revive an abandoned application more than two years after the date of abandonment must provide additional explanation of the circumstances surrounding the delay that establishes the entire delay was unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview procedures and recordation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for conducting interviews (including remote/video), equipment/hosting requirements, and making interview substance of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an examiner is working remotely and no in-person interview is possible, an interview may be conducted via telephone or electronic communication using USPTO web-based collaboration tools. Internet authorization must be submitted on a separate paper to be entitled to acceptance. A video conference is an electronic meeting using USPTO web-based collaboration tools and should be coordinated by the examiner using those tools. Deleted references to specific tools (e.g., WebEx); examiners must only use USPTO-supplied equipment/software for interviews and all video conferences for interviews MUST originate or be hosted by USPTO personnel. Any interview (including any electronic communication that discussed the merits) must be made of record. For applicant-initiated interviews, the substance must be made of record in the reply to an outstanding action or within the set period if no reply is outstanding. Interview Summary form may be provided at end of the interview or mailed to the correspondence address. Proper authority should be on file (submission vs. paper terminology updated) to grant an interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules on who must approve entry of amendments that affect specification disclosure, add claims, or change claim scope, and handling of formal amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recommendation must be forwarded to the supervisory patent examiner (SPE) for consideration and approval for an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 which affects the disclosure of the specification, adds claims, or changes the scope of any claim. An examiner may approve the entry of an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 concerning merely formal matters without the SPE signature. Form PTO-271 (Response to Rule 312 Communication) must be forwarded to the SPE for consideration, approval, and mailing when recommending to enter an amendment in part. Revised related form paragraphs (7.85, 7.86, 7.87).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations and other evidence traversing rejections (37 CFR 1.132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated guidance on affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.132 and treatment of other evidence (including publications) traversing rejections and nexus for objective evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section retitled to indicate it covers affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.132 and other evidence; added discussion that publications may be evidence. Added two new paragraphs discussing requirements for affidavits and declarations and two new paragraphs regarding determining if there is a nexus between the merits of the claimed invention and the asserted objective evidence with citations to Federal Circuit precedent (Fox Factory, Demaco, In re Huang, In re Kao, WBIP v. Kohler, Campbell Soup, Teva v. Eli Lilly). Examiner should indicate an admitted affidavit or declaration on the Office Action Summary, Notice of Allowability, or Advisory Action cover sheet, as appropriate. Added cross references to MPEP §§ 716.01(b) and 2145 for nexus guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting analysis and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified rules and analyses for statutory and nonstatutory double patenting, including what constitutes serious burden and usage of reference patents/applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changed 'common inventor' to 'common (joint) inventor' for consistency. Clarified that the serious burden requirement is a serious 'search and/or examination' burden and added explanation distinguishing serious examination burden from serious search burden and how to demonstrate serious examination burden. Election of species is a type of restriction requirement. Clarified explanations of scenarios in which double patenting may exist; updated basis for double patenting to remove emphasis on order of filing and updated citations (e.g., In re Van Ornum). Added explanation of when copending applications might raise double patenting issues and when an application can be utilized as a double patenting reference. Clarified that subject matter excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) may not be used as a secondary teaching in a nonstatutory double patenting rejection; discussed applicability of benefit claims to patent term filing date; included changes resulting from Patent Law Treaties Implementation Act of 2012 and Uruguay Round Agreement Act. Updated many form paragraphs to align with statutory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice, election of species, and telephone restriction procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on making restriction requirements, election of species rules, handling telephone restrictions, C* classification challenges, and rejoinder/reconsideration procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated process for documenting a telephone restriction, performing a C* classification challenge if required, and incorporating the restriction into the next Office action; clarified that a reviewing primary examiner may approve telephone restrictions by examiners without negotiation authority. Clarified distinctness for restriction requirements and added explanation of serious examination burden and how to demonstrate it. Added explanation of 'mutually exclusive' in restriction context. Revised to clarify that election may include designation of patentably distinct species or a group of patentably indistinct species and that an election of species is subject to same requirements to preserve right to petition as other restriction requirements. Applicant may not disaffirm or change their election as a matter of right after making an oral election and receiving an Office action based upon that oral election (citation to 37 CFR 1.142(b)). Explained when claims ineligible for rejoinder may be canceled by examiner’s amendment and when an amendment canceling all claims drawn to elected invention and presenting only nonelected invention is non-responsive. Added procedures when examiner finds all elected claims allowable following amendment adding claims drawn to a new invention. Reconsideration upon rejoinder of nonelected invention includes reconsidering whether the C* classification picture is correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of references that are patents/applications in double patenting situations
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat reference patents/applications when subject matter is excepted under 102(b)(2)(C) or disqualified under pre-AIA 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New introduction explains this section pertains only to double patenting analysis when subject matter in the reference is excepted as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) or the reference is disqualified as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c). Clarified how to determine common ownership and that, until a reference is excepted/disqualified, an examiner should not apply a double patenting rejection based on a joint research agreement. Clarified timing when common ownership or obligation of assignment must exist for 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) to be applicable. Revised to clarify how applicability of 102(b)(2)(C) or pre-AIA 103(c) affects whether to make a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102/103 or on basis of double patenting. Revised form paragraphs and examiner notes accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and form paragraph updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Updates to multiple form paragraphs and examiner-note language to align with revised policy and statutory language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised many form paragraphs (examples include 7.114, 7.116, 7.118, 7.39.01, 7.100–7.102, 7.82.03, 7.37.05, 7.37.07, 7.37.08, 7.85–7.87, 8.15–8.16, 8.23.02, 8.27–8.37, 8.42–8.50, 7.15.01.aia, and many others) to reflect the substantive changes in rules and practice. Several form paragraphs were relocated or reworded. (This entry captures the broad instruction to use updated form paragraphs as revised throughout the change summary.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology and cross-reference updates (AIA definitions and CFR citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacements of terms and updated cross-references to reflect statutory/regulatory changes (e.g., AIA definition of 'inventor' vs 'applicant', updated CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaced 'applicant derived' with 'inventor derived' and 'applicant’s invention' with 'the claimed invention' to reflect AIA definitions; replaced many references to older forms and rule citations (e.g., PTO/SB/08A and 08B to PTO/SB/08; eRed Folder to action folder; IFW to electronic file) and updated reproduced text of 37 CFR 1.102 and 37 CFR 1.121 to reflect ST.25/ST.26 rulemakings. Also deleted obsolete program references (e.g., Full First Action Interview Pilot Program).
